subject.title: # [Bug]: Installer setup wizard has no Back button

question: Should the gateway wizard support Back navigation through a declarative manifest/final-submit contract, a gateway-owned wizard.back RPC, or another explicit protocol boundary before Windows adds the UI affordance?
rationale: The current Windows client only renders one gateway-owned step at a time, so local Back behavior would require guessing about prior steps, branching, validation, and irreversible side effects.

options.title: Define a declarative wizard manifest
options.body: Have the gateway describe the setup flow up front so Windows can own Back/Forward, draft values, validation checkpoints, and final commit boundaries.

options.title: Add gateway-owned back RPC
options.body: Add wizard.back or wizard.previous semantics to the gateway and then wire Windows Back to that server-owned session state.

options.title: Defer Back navigation
options.body: Keep restart/skip recovery as the supported behavior until the gateway flow is redesigned.

recommendation.title: Define a declarative wizard manifest
recommendation.body: Have the gateway describe the setup flow up front so Windows can own Back/Forward, draft values, validation checkpoints, and final commit boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The collaborator comment already frames the exact protocol choices and this person has nearby setup recovery history.
